latin: Non potest dici quod in intellectu ideae, uerbi gratia, ignis, aquae, et aeris sint tres ideae, sed oportet dicere quod sunt ternarius.
translation: One cannot say that, in the intellect, the ideas of (say) fire, water, and air are three separate ideas; one must instead say that they form a single threefold unity.
translation_note: 'ternarius' = a formal triad, not a set of three discrete individuals (cf. 3>26); sense checked.
